index.title: ComiGo User Manual
index.html:
Download ComiGo ​

The current platform is selected automatically; you can switch the platform and package manually.

Choose how to run ComiGo ​

  • Choose Desktop for a normal application window.
  • Choose Tray for a background service managed from the system tray and read in a browser.
  • Choose the CLI for servers, Docker, or automation.
  • To open a local archive without installing anything, use /reader.

ComiGo serves its Web UI at http://localhost:1234 by default. It scans image directories, archives, PDF, HTML, audio, and video, then selects scroll, flip, or player mode as appropriate.

Scope of this manual ​

This manual follows the current code, comi --help, the ComiGo website, and observed UI behavior. Release history is excluded from Manual search; use GitHub Releases.

Example images use HTTPS URLs and are not bundled into the binary.

Comigo on Omarchy

Use Comigo from the Omarchy status bar: local service controls, remote connections, reading QR codes, and IP selection. Comigo on Omarchy

install.title: Install and choose a build
install.html:
Install and choose a build ​

Pick a build ​

Build Best for Behavior
Desktop A normal application window Hosts the Web UI in Wails; adds system folder selection and can move an eligible local source file to the OS trash after confirmation
Tray A background service read in a browser Tray menu opens or copies the reader URL, opens directories, changes language, checks updates, and manages Tailscale
CLI Servers, Docker, automation, and advanced use comi starts the Web service; an interactive terminal may enter the TUI unless --no-tui is set

Desktop currently has no tray menu or built-in Tailscale. Tray uses the system browser and does not have Wails-only folder selection or source-file trash operations.

GUI downloads ​

These latest URLs match the current comigo.xyz downloader:

System Tray Desktop
Windows x86_64 ZIP ZIP
Windows ARM64 ZIP ZIP
macOS universal DMG DMG
Linux x86_64 tar.gz tar.gz
Linux ARM64 tar.gz tar.gz

macOS says the app is damaged ​

Move the app into Applications first, then clear its download quarantine attribute. Replace the path with the build you installed:

bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/comigo-desktop.app

Install the CLI ​

Choose your operating system and CLI build in the home page download panel, then extract the package. For Linux x86_64:

bash
curl -fL -o comi.tar.gz https://comigo.xyz/yumenaka/comigo/releases/download/latest/comi_latest_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz
tar -xzf comi.tar.gz
./comi --help

Use the matching package for other systems. Run comi after extracting it (comi.exe on Windows), or place it in a directory on PATH.

Update ​

The CLI can check and replace itself through the website proxy:

bash
comi --upgrade

Stop other ComiGo instances first and make sure the executable directory is writable. GUI builds can be updated by installing the newer package over the old one.

quick-start.title: Quick start
quick-start.html:
Quick start ​

Open a book or library ​

The CLI accepts files and directories:

bash
# Scan the current directory as a library
comi .

# Open one book temporarily; file-only arguments skip config file reads and writes
comi book.cbz

# Set a port and pass multiple sources
comi -p 8080 /path/to/manga another-book.pdf

Open http://localhost:1234 after startup. Windows opens the browser by default; elsewhere, copy an address printed in the terminal. To force ordinary server mode without the TUI:

bash
comi --no-tui /path/to/manga

Finish setup in the Web UI ​

  1. Open the right drawer, then Settings.
  2. Add local directories or remote URLs under Libraries.
  3. Wait for scanning; use per-library or global rescan when needed.
  4. Select a cover, then change flip or scroll mode from the drawer.

Settings also shows configuration state, scan controls, and live logs. Live logs are diagnostic and are not part of Manual search.

Phones and tablets ​

On the same LAN, scan the drawer QR code or open a LAN address printed by ComiGo. Opening the drawer refreshes a stale QR code for the current page.

To allow only the current machine:

bash
comi --local /path/to/manga

--local binds to 127.0.0.1, so other devices cannot connect.

Login protection ​

When both username and password are non-empty, the shelf, readers, settings, and protected APIs require login. The Manual, login page, health check, and installer proxy remain public.

bash
comi --username comigo --password 'replace-this' /path/to/manga

Avoid putting a real password in shared shell history; use a protected config file or controlled environment variables for long-running deployments.

reading.title: Reading and offline reader
reading.html:
Reading and offline reader ​

Reading modes ​

Image books have two primary modes:

  • Flip shows a page or spread at a time.
  • Scroll provides continuous vertical reading and configurable loading behavior.

Audio and video use player mode. A single-file HTML book is served directly so an outer reader template does not break its structure or scripts.

The right drawer contains reading mode, crop and resize options, direction, history, QR code, theme, and language. Browser-specific preferences live in local storage; clearing site data or choosing Reset local settings removes them.

Progress, bookmarks, and synchronization ​

During online reading, ComiGo stores automatic progress and user bookmarks. Open reading history from the drawer or Settings to page through or remove records. WebSocket and SSE carry progress and UI updates between pages connected to the same service; proxy and network support still determine whether those channels work.

Remote ComiGo bookmark requests preserve their remote-library key so they cannot collide with a local book of the same name.

Image processing ​

Readers can crop borders and resize images on demand. Cache improves repeat reads but consumes disk space. Remote PDFs are downloaded on demand because PDF processing requires random file access.

For incorrectly decoded ZIP filenames, choose an encoding:

bash
comi --zip-encode shiftjis book.zip

Offline /reader ​

/reader runs locally in the browser:

  1. Open the page and select a ZIP, CBZ, RAR, or CBR file.
  2. The browser and bundled WASM read the file; it is not uploaded to ComiGo.
  3. Supported browsers can install the page as a PWA.

The offline reader has no server library, cross-device history, remote resources, or server-side downloads. The browser must support the required WebAssembly and file APIs.

Downloads and portable reading ​

Depending on book type, the online drawer offers the original file, a ZIP made from an image directory, EPUB conversion, or a single-file portable HTML. Portable HTML includes the static reader and content for transfer or offline use. Video, audio, book groups, and HTML cannot be converted to EPUB.

library.title: Libraries and remote sources
library.html:
Libraries and remote sources ​

Supported content ​

The defaults scan:

  • image directories;
  • .zip, .tar, .rar, .cbz, .cbr, .epub;
  • .pdf;
  • .html, .htm;
  • common video and audio files including MP4, WebM, MP3, AAC, OGG, WAV, and WMA.

Default image types include JPEG, PNG, GIF/APNG, BMP, WebP, HEIC/HEIF, and AVIF. A directory or archive needs at least MinImageNum images, and recursion is limited by MaxScanDepth.

Local libraries ​

Add a directory in Settings or pass it to comi. Relative paths become absolute. A local library cannot be added twice or overlap an existing library as its parent or child.

ExcludePath omits names such as the default node_modules and recycle-bin directories. Rescan after files change, or set AutoRescanIntervalMinutes for periodic scanning.

Remote file systems ​

Supported URL schemes include WebDAV (webdav, dav, davs), SMB, SFTP, S3, FTP, and FTPS:

toml
StoreUrls = [
  "davs://user:pass@example.com/books",
  "smb://user:pass@server/share/books"
]

Credentials embedded in a URL are stored in the config file, so restrict its permissions. Remote connection work obeys the scan timeout and may use the local image cache.

Remote ComiGo ​

An ordinary http:// or https:// home URL is treated as another ComiGo server, not generic WebDAV:

toml
StoreUrls = ["https://reader.example.com"]

The local instance reads the remote index and proxies covers, pages, downloads, and bookmarks on demand. It keeps an index locally but does not retain the original remote files. Include any base path in the home URL, such as https://example.com/comics, and use HTTPS when credentials are present.

Database and metadata ​

By default the library works in memory with JSON persistence. --database enables a database index, using SQLite unless --db-type postgres --db-dsn ... is selected. The database stores indexes and bookmarks; it does not replace or back up source books.

desktop.title: Desktop, tray, and TUI
desktop.html:
Desktop, tray, and TUI ​

Desktop (Wails) ​

Desktop runs the same ComiGo Web UI in a dedicated application window. It adds native directory selection, fullscreen control, and an operation to trash a local source file.

Delete source file requires page confirmation and only accepts a real file inside a configured local library. Directories, book groups, remote books, and paths outside the library are rejected. If the OS trash facility is unavailable, ComiGo returns an error instead of permanently deleting the file. The index is updated only after the move succeeds.

Desktop currently has no tray menu and no built-in Tailscale.

Tray ​

Tray starts a background Web service and opens the system browser. Its menu can open or copy the reader URL, open config and library directories, change language, check updates, and manage Tailscale on supported systems.

Closing a browser tab does not stop the service; exit from the tray menu. Configuration profiles are separated by host: tray uses tray.toml, desktop uses desktop.toml, and ordinary CLI uses config.toml.

CLI and TUI ​

In an interactive terminal the CLI may show a TUI for browsing the library, previewing covers, and opening the terminal reader. Image quality depends on terminal protocols and fonts; Kitty-compatible terminals generally provide the fullest support.

Disable it for servers, systemd, containers, and non-interactive use:

bash
comi --no-tui /data

Which one should I use? ​

  • One-machine app: Desktop.
  • Always-on home LAN service: Tray.
  • NAS, cloud server, or container: CLI with --no-tui.

They share reader and library logic, but host capabilities differ. Do not assume Wails-only menus or deletion behavior exist in browser and tray builds.

Comigo on Omarchy

Use Comigo from the Omarchy status bar: local service controls, remote connections, reading QR codes, and IP selection. Comigo on Omarchy

deployment.title: Deployment and configuration
deployment.html:
Deployment and configuration ​

Common CLI flags ​

These values come from the current comi --help:

Flag Default Purpose
-p, --port 1234 Web port
--base-path empty Reverse-proxy base such as /comics
--local false Listen only on this machine
-n, --no-tui false Disable the TUI
-t, --temp automatic Temporary reading without config file I/O
--username / --password empty Enable login when both are set
--read-only false Block Web config changes and upload
--database false Enable database indexing
--db-type sqlite sqlite or postgres
--auto-rescan-min 0 Periodic scan interval; 0 disables it
--tailscale false Built-in Tailscale, except Desktop
--tls / --auto-tls false Existing certificate or Let's Encrypt

Run comi --help for the complete current list.

Config files ​

CLI, Desktop, and Tray use config.toml, desktop.toml, and tray.toml. ComiGo searches the user config, working, and program directories for the matching profile; --config selects an explicit path. Settings shows the loaded locations and can save a profile.

toml
Port = 1234
Language = "auto"
StoreUrls = ["/data/books"]
MaxScanDepth = 4
MinImageNum = 3
EnableUpload = false
ReadOnlyMode = true
Username = "comigo"
Password = "change-me"
BasePath = "/comics"

Docker ​

bash
docker run -d \
  --name comigo \
  -p 1234:1234 \
  -v /path/to/books:/data \
  yumenaka/comigo:latest

Use --no-tui inside containers. Mount /root/.config/comigo only when config persistence is needed. Prefer read-only mounts for libraries that must not change, and consider authentication and disk limits before enabling upload.

Reverse proxy and base path ​

For an external URL such as https://example.com/comics/, configure the proxy consistently and run:

bash
comi --no-tui --base-path /comics /data

The health check becomes /comics/healthz. Application pages, APIs, PWA paths, and QR URLs use the base path; Manual stays at the root /manual/. Proxy WebSocket and SSE or progress sync, live logs, and scan notifications may fail.

TLS, login, and remote access ​

  • --tls --tls-crt ... --tls-key ... uses an existing certificate.
  • --auto-tls --host comics.example.com obtains a Let's Encrypt certificate and listens on 443.
  • Non-empty username and password enable JWT-cookie login.
  • --tailscale starts tsnet; keep password enforcement when Funnel exposes the service publicly.

Manual is intentionally public and bypasses login. Never put passwords, private addresses, or real credential-bearing URLs in documentation.

OPDS ​

OPDS 1.2 clients can connect to /opds. With authentication enabled, OPDS belongs to the protected routes and the client must support the required Cookie or JWT access.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.html:
FAQ ​

Why is a book missing? ​

Make sure the path exists on the machine or inside the container, then check MaxScanDepth, MinImageNum, ExcludePath, and supported extensions. Container host paths must be mounted to the path ComiGo sees. Rescan after changes.

Why can my phone not connect? ​

Do not use the phone's own localhost. Use the LAN address printed by ComiGo or shown in its QR code, and allow the port through the firewall. --local binds only to 127.0.0.1 and intentionally blocks other devices.

Why do assets return 404 behind a proxy? ​

The proxy path and --base-path must agree. External /comics/ means --base-path /comics. Forward WebSocket and SSE, and do not add the same prefix twice.

ZIP filenames are garbled ​

Try --zip-encode gbk, --zip-encode shiftjis, or set ZipFileTextEncoding. Converting the archive filenames to UTF-8 at the source is the most reliable fix.

Why is a remote library slow? ​

The first scan reads directories and metadata. Cache improves repeat reads; a longer timeout only tolerates a slow connection and does not add bandwidth. Remote PDFs must be downloaded on demand for parsing. Remote ComiGo is usually better suited to cross-network use than scanning each file over a generic protocol.

Does clearing cache delete source books? ​

No. Delete book cache removes metadata and cache only. Desktop has a separate, confirmed Delete source file action which moves eligible files inside local libraries to the OS trash; other builds do not provide it.

Why is release history absent? ​

Manual search describes current behavior only. See GitHub Releases and commit history for version changes.

How do I report a problem? ​

Inspect live logs in Settings or enable --debug. Remove passwords, credential-bearing URLs, file names, and other private data, then open a GitHub issue with version, platform, startup command, and reproduction steps.

comigo-omarchy.title: Comigo on Omarchy
comigo-omarchy.html:
Comigo on Omarchy

Install the panel

comigo-omarchy is a native Omarchy status bar panel for Comigo. It requires Omarchy with shell plugin support, Bash, curl, and a Comigo v1.3.5 or later server. A local CLI is required only for local mode. The panel offers English, Chinese, and Japanese.

omarchy plugin add https://github.com/yumenaka/comigo-omarchy --enable

Click the status bar icon to open the plugin. Its ID is yumenaka.comigo. Overview shows reading links and QR codes; Status shows service and traffic data; Service manages the local CLI and updates; Settings handles connections, login, and configuration.

Connect to a local library

  1. Select Local and open Settings. If the CLI is missing, Service offers an install button that downloads the matching release from comigo.xyz, then starts Comigo automatically without changing the current page.
  2. Enter the loopback URL, normally http://127.0.0.1:1234/. Match the actual protocol, port, and BasePath, such as http://127.0.0.1:1234/books/.
  3. Leave the CLI path empty to search PATH for comi or comigo, or specify its full path. Leave the library empty to use Comigo defaults, or select an existing directory.
  4. Save, then start Comigo on Service. Log in on Settings if requested.

The URL configures the panel connection, not the server port or TLS. The plugin runs comi --no-tui --open-browser=false, passing a library argument only when configured. Comigo loads its own configuration. The config file card shows the actual file and opens Web settings for file management.

The CLI installer uses /usr/bin/comi when /usr/bin is on PATH, otherwise ~/.local/bin/comi. A system-directory write requests administrator authentication. Existing targets are not overwritten.

Without library arguments or a configuration file, Comigo selects the first existing directory under Home in this order: Pictures, Documents, Downloads. If none exists, it uses the working directory; it does not create these directories.

Read and choose an IP

Overview starts with the server-provided reading URL, normally its outbound interface IP. With external access enabled and multiple local IPs available, use the arrows beside the QR code to cycle them. The URL, QR code, and open/copy actions follow the selection; the current IP is bold. IPv6 and the URL protocol, port, and path are retained. Polling keeps an available selection. Local-only mode does not offer IP switching.

To read from another device, enable external access in Settings and select an IP reachable from that device. Changing the listener reconnects the panel. On a read-only server this setting cannot be changed.

Use a remote server

Select Remote, enter the full HTTP(S) home URL, including BasePath, and save. For example, use https://reader.example/books/. The server must already be running and reachable; log in if required.

All pages show remote data. Reading links and QR codes retain the configured URL. Local process control, installation, logs, CLI/library paths, LAN and firewall controls, and IP cycling are unavailable. Local and remote URLs and login sessions are separate. Switching mode does not start or stop services; Shell startup defaults to Local.

Service lifecycle and automatic startup

Only processes started and recorded by the plugin can be stopped by it. If another service owns the port, manage that service through its own launcher. Closing the panel or restarting Shell does not stop Comigo.

Automatic startup is off by default. Enable it on Service to start the local CLI when the plugin loads, including the current session. It uses no systemd service. Failures retry at intervals of at least 10 seconds, up to three attempts per login session. Plugin or Shell reloads preserve the budget. Success or manual process control ends automatic attempts for that session; disabling the switch cancels further retries. Start manually after the limit.

LAN firewall access

With UFW installed and enabled, Settings can allow the current TCP port from the default interface’s directly connected private IPv4 subnet. The operation requests administrator authentication. Revocation deletes only rules marked omarchy-comigo, preserving user rules. Check the selected IP, network isolation, and firewall if another device cannot connect; a configured rule alone does not establish reachability.

Saved settings and updates

Settings are stored in ~/.config/omarchy-comigo/settings.json, or under XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set. Passwords and tokens are not saved there. Authentication sessions remain in memory, separated by mode and URL; log in again after a Shell restart or token expiry. External settings changes preserve edited drafts.

Complete status refreshes about every 30 seconds; an open panel refreshes traffic every two seconds, and Settings fetches running configuration at that interval. Traffic measures the current Comigo process’s HTTP bodies and resets when it restarts.

Update checks show the release page and a copyable upgrade command; they do not install updates. A stopped local service uses comi desktop check-update. Restart Comigo after upgrading. Check local desktop support with comi desktop info; its protocol is 1.

Troubleshooting and removal

  • Offline: match the URL with the actual service configuration and inspect Service logs.
  • No IP arrows: select Local, enable external access, and confirm multiple available IPs.
  • Disabled login: anonymous servers enable login controls only when authentication is needed or a session exists.
  • Installed UI not visible: run omarchy restart shell and reopen the panel.

To remove a GitHub-installed plugin:

omarchy plugin remove yumenaka.comigo

For a local checkout installed with bash install.sh, run bash install.sh --uninstall from that checkout. Removal preserves books and settings and does not stop Comigo. Stop a plugin-managed service first if needed. See the plugin README for source installation, shortcuts, logs, and development checks.
